problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the 1870s, most American cities relied on horse-drawn streetcars, which were slow and limited by the animals' endurance.
- Frank Sprague developed a reliable electric streetcar system in Richmond, Virginia, in 1888, using overhead wires to power the cars.
- Sprague's system allowed streetcars to travel faster and farther than horse-drawn cars without tiring, cutting commute times significantly.
- Within a few years, dozens of cities adopted electric streetcar systems modeled on Sprague's design.
- The expanded range of electric streetcars allowed workers to live farther from city centers, contributing to the growth of early suburbs.
- Before electric streetcars, most workers had to live within walking distance of factories or horse-car lines.
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the 1870s, most American cities relied on horse-drawn streetcars, which were slow and limited by the animals' endurance.
- Frank Sprague developed a reliable electric streetcar system in Richmond, Virginia, in 1888, using overhead wires to power the cars.
- Sprague's system allowed streetcars to travel faster and farther than horse-drawn cars without tiring, cutting commute times significantly.
- Within a few years, dozens of cities adopted electric streetcar systems modeled on Sprague's design.
- The expanded range of electric streetcars allowed workers to live farther from city centers, contributing to the growth of early suburbs.
- Before electric streetcars, most workers had to live within walking distance of factories or horse-car lines.
problem.question: The student wants to explain how Sprague's electric streetcar system changed where American workers could live. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Sprague's 1888 system in Richmond used overhead wires to power streetcars, replacing the horse-drawn cars that had limited urban transportation for decades.

Because Sprague's electric streetcars could travel farther and faster than horse-drawn cars, workers who had once needed to live within walking distance of their jobs could now live in farther suburbs.
Dozens of cities adopted electric streetcar systems modeled on Sprague's design within just a few years of its introduction in Richmond, Virginia.
Horse-drawn streetcars were slow and limited by the animals' endurance, which made commuting difficult for many workers in the 1870s.
problem.explanation: 학생의 목표는 스프레이그의 전기 노면전차가 '노동자들이 어디에 살 수 있는지'를 어떻게 바꿨는지 설명하는 것이다. 이는 예전에는 노동자들이 도보 거리 내에 살아야 했다는 조건(note 6), 전기 노면전차가 더 빠르고 멀리 이동할 수 있게 했다는 사실(note 3), 그 결과 교외에 살 수 있게 되었다는 결론(note 5)을 모두 연결해야 한다. B는 이 세 요소를 인과적으로 정확히 연결한다. A는 시스템의 기술적 특징만 설명하고 거주지 변화와 연결하지 않는다(note 하나만 사용). C는 다른 도시로의 확산만 다뤄 거주지 문제와 무관하다(목표 무시). D는 말 노면전차의 한계만 설명할 뿐 전기 노면전차 도입 이후의 변화는 다루지 않아 잘못된 note 조합이다.
problem.explanationEn: The student's goal is to explain how Sprague's electric streetcar system changed WHERE workers could live. This requires linking the earlier constraint that workers had to live within walking distance (note 6), the fact that electric streetcars traveled faster and farther (note 3), and the resulting ability to live in suburbs (note 5). Choice B connects all three causally. Choice A only describes the technical features of the system without connecting to where workers lived (uses only one note). Choice C discusses the spread of the technology to other cities, which is irrelevant to the housing question (ignores the goal). Choice D only describes the limitations of horse-drawn cars without addressing the change after electric streetcars were introduced (combines the wrong notes).
problem.evidenceSpan: Sprague's system allowed streetcars to travel faster and farther than horse-drawn cars without tiring, cutting commute times significantly. / The expanded range of electric streetcars allowed workers to live farther from city centers, contributing to the growth of early suburbs. / Before electric streetcars, most workers had to live within walking distance of factories or horse-car lines.
problem.answerRationale: 정답은 전기 노면전차의 속도·거리 향상(원인)과 그로 인해 노동자들이 도보 거리 제한에서 벗어나 교외에 거주할 수 있게 된 결과를 연결한다.

difficultyReasons: 질문의 목표(거주지 변화 설명)에 정확히 부합하는 선택지를 골라야 함
각 오답이 노트의 실제 정보를 활용하고 있어 표면적으로는 그럴듯함
오답들이 사실 관계는 맞지만 질문의 초점(노동자의 거주지 변화)과 어긋난다는 점을 파악해야 함
전후 관계(속도/거리 증가 → 교외 거주 가능)를 정확히 연결해야 함

distractors.plausibleBecause: Sprague의 시스템에 대한 사실적 정보를 담고 있어 관련성이 있어 보인다
distractors.matches: Sprague의 1888년 리치몬드 시스템, 가공 전선, 말이 끄는 차량 대체
distractors.whyWrong: 노동자들이 어디에 살 수 있는지에 대한 변화를 설명하지 않고 단순히 기술 도입 사실만 서술한다

distractors.plausibleBecause: Sprague의 시스템이 확산된 사실을 다루고 있어 관련 있어 보인다
distractors.matches: 수년 내 여러 도시가 Sprague의 설계를 채택했다는 정보
distractors.whyWrong: 도시 확산 속도만 설명할 뿐 노동자의 거주지 변화와는 직접 연결되지 않는다

distractors.plausibleBecause: 1870년대 통근의 어려움을 설명하여 배경 지식처럼 보인다
distractors.matches: 말이 끄는 차량의 느림과 한계, 1870년대 통근 어려움
distractors.whyWrong: 전기 streetcar 도입 이전 상황만 설명할 뿐 Sprague의 시스템이 가져온 변화(더 먼 곳에 거주 가능)를 언급하지 않는다
